chip.$description: Interactive small pill — the checkbox-like sibling deliberately split from Badge (display-only). Two kinds sharing one shell (radius/size/icon-slot): 'toggle' (filter selection — click flips checked/unchecked, e.g. 'I'm Involved'/'Flagged'/'Expires Soon') and 'removable' (a selected value with a trailing dismiss — e.g. a chosen option in a multi-select, a recipient chip). Same ARIA-role-driven split reasoning as Menu/Listbox and Badge/Chip themselves: a toggle is checkbox-like, a removable chip is a dismissible tag, neither is a passive status display (that's Badge). Sizes sit one rung between Badge (16/20/24) and Button (32/40/48) on purpose — a chip is clickable like a button but reads as a small pill like Badge, so its height ladder (24/32/40) is literally Button's own ladder shifted down one dim-step (dim.6/8/10) at every size.

size.$description: Label composed directly from typography primitives (weight.semibold, leading.none) rather than a text-style.* alias — same reasoning Badge/Counter/Avatar's own labels already established: reading-paragraph leading adds vertical air a tight pill doesn't have room for.

toggle.$description: Filter-selection chip — click flips checked/unchecked, exactly the Checkbox/Radio/Switch mental model in pill form. 'checkedOutline' is a second checked treatment, not a state ladder rung: use it (instead of solid 'checked') when the chip carries a Counter — a chip summarizing 'N sub-selections inside' (e.g. a 'Filters' trigger chip showing the drawer's active-filter count) is an aggregate/trigger, not a single boolean, so filling it fully solid would overstate it. Solid checked = a real one-thing-is-on toggle (no counter). Outline checked reuses Badge's own tint recipe (bg.primary+text.primary) plus a border for the extra definition an interactive element needs that a passive Badge doesn't.

hover.$description: fill.primary, not border.strong — same 'plain gray reads as too weak a cue' lesson Checkbox/Radio/Card's own unchecked-hover already applied. Toggle-specific: this previews 'clicking turns this on', which a passive removable chip's hover never means (see removable.hover below).

disabled.$description: Unchecked disabled — bg/border stay default's, only text/icon fade, same 'disabled keeps its background' convention as Button/Input/Checkbox.

removable.$description: A selected value with a trailing dismiss (×) — a chosen multi-select option, a recipient/tag chip. Existence IS the selection; there's no checked/unchecked ladder, only present-or-removed. Shares 'toggle.default''s exact visual (bg/border/text/icon) on purpose — both read as 'a quiet chip sitting on the page' at rest, no reason to invent a second resting look.

hover.$description: Plain border.strong, deliberately NOT fill.primary — a removable chip isn't a toggle, hovering its body doesn't mean 'clicking turns this blue', so it gets the ordinary Card-style hover, not the toggle-specific activation cue.

remove.$description: The trailing (×) button's own recipe — resolved from Popover/Drawer/Modal's own close-button tokens, not retyped: transparent → fill.neutralHover → fill.neutralActive, icon.secondary at rest.

focus.$description: Shared by both kinds — same system-wide ring (border.focus, dim.1 width, dim.0_5 offset) every focusable component uses.
